translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the fifth month of the seventh year, officials reported: "At Ninghua Town in En Prefecture, beside the Great River, the ground is low and lies directly in the path of a crushing bend in the current.

sentences.zh: 歲久堤岸怯薄，沁水透堤甚多，近鎮居民例皆移避。

translations.literal: Over the years the dikes have grown thin and weak; seeping water penetrates the dikes in many places, and residents near the town all remove and flee as a rule.
translations.idiomatic: Years of wear had left the banks thin and brittle; water seeped through in countless places, and townsfolk had long since abandoned the vicinity.

sentences.zh: 方秋夏之交，時雨霈然，一失堤防，則不惟東流莫測所向，一隅生靈所系甚大，亦恐妨阻大名、河間諸州往來邊路。

translations.literal: At the turn of autumn and summer, when rains fall in abundance, if the dikes fail once, then not only will the eastern flow's course be unpredictable, but the lives tied to one corner of land weigh very greatly; there is also fear of blocking the frontier routes by which Daming, Hejian, and other prefectures travel back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: With the rainy season between summer and autumn, a single breach would send the eastern flow surging on an unknown course—endangering a whole district of lives—and might also cut the frontier highways linking Daming, Hejian, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 乞付有司，貼築固護。」

translations.literal: I beg that it be handed to the responsible offices to face-build and strengthen in protection."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the proper offices be ordered to reinforce the banks in place."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The order was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 六月癸酉，都水使者孟揚言：「舊河陽南北兩河分流，立中氵單，系浮梁。

translations.literal: In the sixth month on the day guiyou, the Commissioner of Waterways Meng Yang said: "Formerly at Heyang the northern and southern rivers divided their flow; a middle pontoon was erected and a floating bridge was secured.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou in the sixth month, Waterways Commissioner Meng Yang reported: "At Heyang the northern and southern branches once split the flow, with a central pontoon anchoring a floating bridge.

sentences.zh: 頃緣北河淤澱，水不通行，止于南河修系一橋。

translations.literal: Recently, because the northern river silted and deposited, water could not pass through; it stopped at repairing and securing a single bridge on the southern river.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the northern branch has silted shut and no longer carries water; only the southern branch still bears a bridge.

sentences.zh: 因此河項窄狹，水勢沖激，每遇漲水，多致損壞。

translations.literal: For this reason the river stretch is narrow and constricted; the water's force rushes and strikes; whenever flood water comes, damage is often caused.
translations.idiomatic: That stretch is narrow, and the current hammers it; every flood season the bridge suffers repeated damage.

sentences.zh: 欲措置開修北河，如舊修系南北兩橋。」

translations.literal: We wish to arrange and open and repair the northern river, repairing and securing northern and southern bridges as of old."
translations.idiomatic: We propose reopening the northern channel and restoring both bridges as before."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The order was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 九月丁未，詔揚專一措置，而令河陽守臣王序營辦錢糧，督其工料。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on the day dingwei, an edict ordered Yang to take sole charge of arrangements, while ordering Heyang's guarding official Wang Xu to provision funds and grain and supervise the labor and materials.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the ninth month the court put Yang in sole charge of the work and ordered Heyang prefect Wang Xu to supply funds and oversee labor and materials.

sentences.zh: 重和元年三月己亥，詔：「滑州、浚州界萬年堤，全藉林木固護堤岸，其廣行種植，以壯地勢。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Chonghe, third month, day jihai, an edict: "The Wannian Dike on the border of Huazhou and Xunzhou relies entirely on forest trees to protect the dike banks; broadly plant trees along it to strengthen the terrain's force."
translations.idiomatic: On jihai in the third month of the first year of Chonghe, an edict ran: "The Wannian Dike along the Huazhou–Xunzhou border depends wholly on timber to hold its banks—plant trees widely along it to buttress the ground."

sentences.zh: 五月甲辰，詔：「孟州河陽縣第一埽，自春以來，河勢湍猛，侵齧民田，迫近州城止二三里。

translations.literal: In the fifth month on the day jiachen, an edict: "The first revetment in Heyang County, Mengzhou, since spring the river's force has been swift and fierce, gnawing and invading commoners' fields, pressing close to the prefectural city by only two or three li.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen in the fifth month another edict said: "At the first revetment in Heyang County, Mengzhou, since spring the river has run fierce, eating into farmland and closing to within two or three li of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 其令都水使者同漕臣、河陽守臣措置固護。」

translations.literal: Order the Commissioner of Waterways together with the transport official and Heyang's guarding official to arrange and strengthen in protection."
translations.idiomatic: Let the Waterways Commissioner, the transport commissioner, and the Heyang prefect coordinate reinforcement."

sentences.zh: 是秋雨，廣武埽危急，詔內侍王仍相度措置。

translations.literal: That autumn it rained; the Guangwu revetment was critically endangered; an edict ordered the inner attendant Wang Reng to survey and arrange measures.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn rains endangered the Guangwu revetment; the court sent palace attendant Wang Reng to survey and manage the crisis.

sentences.zh: 二年九月己卯，王黼言：「昨孟昌齡計議河事，至滑州韓村埽檢視，河流沖至寸金潭，其勢就下，未易禦遏。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year on the day jimao, Wang Fu said: "Yesterday Meng Changling planned river matters; at Hancun revetment in Huazhou he inspected; the river's flow rushed to Cunjin Pool; its force ran downward and was not easy to hold back and stop.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao in the ninth month of the second year, Wang Fu reported: "When Meng Changling surveyed the river at Hancun revetment in Huazhou, the current had driven into Cunjin Pool—the descent was steep and nearly impossible to contain.

sentences.zh: 近降詔旨，令就畫定港灣，對開直河。

translations.literal: Recently an edict was issued ordering that at the drawn and fixed harbor bend, a straight river be opened opposite.
translations.idiomatic: A recent edict had ordered a channel cut straight across the mapped harbor bend.

sentences.zh: 方議開鑿，忽自成直河一道，寸金潭下，水即安流，在役之人，聚首仰歎。

translations.literal: Just when opening and digging was under discussion, suddenly a straight river course formed by itself; below Cunjin Pool the water at once flowed calmly; those on the labor teams gathered their heads and looked up and sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: While crews debated excavation, a straight channel suddenly formed of its own; below Cunjin Pool the water steadied at once, and laborers raised their heads and marveled.

sentences.zh: 乞付史館，仍帥百官表賀。」

translations.literal: I beg that it be sent to the Historiographical Institute, and still lead the hundred officials in a congratulatory memorial."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the event be recorded in the Historical Archives and that all officials be led in congratulatory memorials."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The order was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，河溢冀州信都。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, the river overflowed Xindu in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year the river flooded Xindu in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，河決清河埽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the river broke at Qinghe revetment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the river burst at Qinghe revetment.

sentences.zh: 是歲，水壞天成、聖功橋，官吏行罰有差。

translations.literal: That year, water damaged the Tiancheng and Shenggong bridges; officials and clerks received differentiated punishments according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: That year floods wrecked the Tiancheng and Shenggong bridges; responsible officials were punished according to their degree of fault.

sentences.zh: 四年四月壬子，都水使者孟揚言：「奉詔修系三山東橋，凡役工十五萬七千八百，今累經漲水無虞。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year, fourth month, day renzi, the Commissioner of Waterways Meng Yang said: "In obedience to an edict we repaired and secured the Sanshandong Bridge; in all corvée laborers numbered 157,800; now after repeated flood seasons there is no cause for concern."
translations.idiomatic: On renzi in the fourth month of the fourth year, Waterways Commissioner Meng Yang reported: "By imperial order we restored the Sanshandong Bridge, employing 157,800 laborers; it has since weathered repeated floods without trouble."

sentences.zh: 詔因橋壞失職降秩者，俱復之，揚自正議大夫轉正奉大夫。

translations.literal: An edict: those who had lost office and been demoted in rank because of bridge damage—all were restored; Yang advanced from Rectifier of Discussion to Rectifier of Tributary.
translations.idiomatic: The throne restored officials demoted for the bridge disaster; Yang was promoted from Rectifier of Discussion to Rectifier of Tributary.

sentences.zh: 七年，欽宗即位。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Qinzong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Qinzong succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年二月乙卯，御史中丞許翰言：「保和殿大學士孟昌齡、延康殿學士孟揚、龍圖閣直學士孟揆，父子相繼領職二十年，過惡山積。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, second month, day yimao, the Censor-in-Chief Xu Han said: "Baohé Hall Academician Meng Changling, Yankang Hall Academician Meng Yang, Longtu Pavilion Direct Academician Meng Kui—father and sons in succession held office twenty years; transgressions and wrongs piled mountain-high.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the second month of the first year of Jingkang, Censor-in-Chief Xu Han impeached the Mengs: "Baohé Academician Meng Changling, Yankang Academician Meng Yang, and Longtu Direct Academician Meng Kui held river office in succession for twenty years, piling wrong upon wrong.

sentences.zh: 妄設堤防之功，多張梢樁之數，窮竭民力，聚斂金帛。

translations.literal: Falsely setting up achievements in dike defense, greatly inflating the number of pile-stakes, exhausting the people's strength, amassing gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: They invented dike works and inflated stake counts, exhausting the people and hoarding gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 交結權要，內侍王仍為之奧主，超付名位，不知紀極。

translations.literal: They associated with powerful favorites; the inner attendant Wang Reng was their patron within, leap-frogging them into name and rank beyond all measure.
translations.idiomatic: They trafficked with court favorites; palace attendant Wang Reng was their shadow patron, catapulting them through ranks beyond reason.

sentences.zh: 大河浮橋，歲一造舟，京西之民，猶憚其役。

translations.literal: On the Great River floating bridge, each year boats are newly built once; people of Jingxi still fear this corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The Great River pontoon bridge required new boats every year, and western capital corvée districts still dread the duty.

sentences.zh: 而昌齡首建三山之策，回大河之勢，頓取百年浮橋之費，僅為數歲行路之觀。

translations.literal: Yet Changling first established the Sanshan plan, turning the Great River's force, suddenly taking a century's worth of floating-bridge expense for merely a few years' spectacle of travel on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Changling's Sanshan scheme diverted the main current, squandering a century of floating-bridge costs on a few years of ceremonial thoroughfare.

sentences.zh: 漂沒生靈，無慮萬計，近輔郡縣，蕭然破殘。

translations.literal: Lives drowned and lost, numbering no less than in the tens of thousands; prefectures and counties near the capital were bleakly broken and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Countless thousands drowned; neighboring prefectures lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 所辟官吏，計金敘績，富商大賈，爭注名牒，身不在公，遙分爵賞。

translations.literal: Officials they recruited reckoned gold in grading achievements; great merchants and peddlers vied to register their names on rosters; their persons were not at court, yet from afar they partitioned rank and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Hirelings they picked were paid by the purse; wealthy contractors queued for nominal posts and drew honors without ever attending court.

sentences.zh: 每興一役，幹沒無數，省部御史，莫能鉤考。

translations.literal: Each time one labor project was launched, embezzlement was without number; the ministries and the censorate could not investigate and audit.
translations.idiomatic: Every project they launched bred bottomless graft, beyond the reach of ministry auditors or the censorate.

sentences.zh: 陛下方將澄清朝著，建立事功，不先誅竄昌齡父子，無以昭示天下。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is now about to clarify the court roster and establish achievements in affairs; unless Changling father and sons are first executed and banished, there is no means to show it to All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: As Your Majesty sets the court in order, the Mengs must be punished first—or justice will never convince the realm.

sentences.zh: 望籍其奸贓，以正典刑。」

translations.literal: I look to register their treacherous gains and apply the proper penal statutes.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that their ill-gotten gains be inventoried and standard penalties applied.

sentences.zh: 詔並落職：昌齡在外宮觀，揚依舊權領都水監職事，揆候措置橋船畢取旨。

translations.literal: An edict demoted all in office: Changling to outer palace attendance, Yang as before provisionally to head Directorate of Waterways duties, Kui to await finishing bridge-boat arrangements then receive instructions.
translations.idiomatic: All three were demoted: Changling to an outer palace post, Yang retained interim charge of the Directorate of Waterways, Kui to finish pontoon work before further orders.

sentences.zh: 翰復請鉤考簿書，發其奸贓。

translations.literal: Han again requested to investigate and audit account books and expose their treacherous gains.
translations.idiomatic: Han again asked to audit their accounts and expose their corruption.

sentences.zh: 乃詔昌齡與中大夫，揚、揆與中奉大夫。

translations.literal: Then an edict: Changling with Junior Grandee of Grace, Yang and Kui with Junior Master of Grace for Tributary.
translations.idiomatic: The court instead granted Changling Junior Grandee of Grace and Yang and Kui Junior Master of Grace for Tributary—mild ranks after denunciation.

sentences.zh: 三月丁丑，京西轉運司言：「本路歲科河防夫三萬，溝河夫一萬八千。

translations.literal: In the third month on the day dingchou, the Jingxi Transport Office said: "On this circuit each year corvée for river defense numbered 30,000; for ditch-river corvée 18,000.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou in the third month the Jingxi transport commissioner reported: "This circuit levies 30,000 corvée laborers yearly for river defense and 18,000 for canal work.

sentences.zh: 緣連年不稔，群盜劫掠，民力困弊，乞量數減放。」

translations.literal: Because in successive years harvests have not been ripe, bandits plunder, the people's strength is exhausted and damaged; I beg to measure and reduce the numbers released.
translations.idiomatic: Years of failed harvests and bandit raids have broken the populace; we beg a measured reduction.

sentences.zh: 詔減八千人。

translations.literal: An edict reduced by eight thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: The court cut the levy by eight thousand laborers.

sentences.zh: 汴河，自隋大業初，疏通濟渠，引黃河通淮，至唐，改名廣濟。

translations.literal: The Bian Canal—in the beginning of the Sui Great Enterprise era, the Ji Channel was dredged and opened, drawing the Yellow River to connect with the Huai; reaching the Tang, its name was changed to Guangji.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian Canal: in early Sui, engineers dredged the Ji Channel to draw Yellow River water toward the Huai; under Tang it was renamed Guangji.

sentences.zh: 宋都大樑，以孟州河陰縣南為汴首受黃河之口，屬於淮、泗。

translations.literal: The Song capital at Daliang takes south of Heyin County, Mengzhou, as the Bian's head to receive the Yellow River's mouth, belonging to the Huai and Si.
translations.idiomatic: The Song seat at Daliang took the Yellow River intake south of Heyin in Mengzhou as the canal head, feeding the Huai and Si systems.

sentences.zh: 每歲自春及冬，常於河口均調水勢，止深六尺，以通行重載為准。

translations.literal: Each year from spring through winter, at the river mouth water force is evenly regulated, stopping depth at six chi, taking passage of heavy loads as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: From spring through winter officials balanced the intake so depth held at six chi—enough for heavy grain barges.

sentences.zh: 歲漕江、淮、湖、浙米數百萬，及至東南之產，百物眾寶，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Each year grain transported from Jiang, Huai, Lake, and Zhe numbered in the millions; reaching products of the southeast, the hundred things and multitudinous treasures are countless completely.
translations.idiomatic: Millions of bushels from the Jianghuai and Zhe regions arrived annually, with southeast luxuries beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 又下西山之薪炭，以輸京師之粟，以振河北之急，內外仰給焉。

translations.literal: Again fuel and charcoal from western mountains are sent down to transport capital grain, to relieve Hebei's urgency; inside and outside depend on its supply.
translations.idiomatic: Western Hills charcoal rode the same waterway to feed the capital and Hebei's emergencies—the realm depended on this conduit.

sentences.zh: 故于諸水，莫此為重。

translations.literal: Therefore among all waters, none is heavier than this.
translations.idiomatic: Among rivers none weighed heavier in statecraft.

sentences.zh: 其淺深有度，置官以司之，都水監總察之。

translations.literal: Its shallow depth and deep depth have standards; officials are established to oversee it, and the Directorate of Waterways inspects and oversees them in total.
translations.idiomatic: Depth was regulated by statute; canal officers answered to the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 然大河向背不常，故河口歲易；

translations.literal: But the Great River's facing and turning are not constant; therefore the river mouth changes every year;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Yellow River's course shifted; the intake moved almost yearly;

sentences.zh: 易則度地形，相水勢，為口以逆之。

translations.literal: when it changes then measuring terrain and comparing water force, a mouth is made to meet it in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: and each time officials had to read the land and bend a new mouth against the current.

sentences.zh: 遇春首輒調數州之民，勞費不貲，役者多溺死。

translations.literal: Meeting the turn of spring, corvée from several prefectures is always conscripted; labor expense is beyond reckoning, and many on the labor teams drown and die.
translations.idiomatic: Every spring brought corvée from several prefectures at ruinous cost—workers often drowned.

sentences.zh: 吏又並緣侵漁，而京師常有決溢之虞。

translations.literal: Clerks again take opportunity to encroach and embezzle, while the capital constantly has the anxiety of breach and overflow.
translations.idiomatic: Officials fattened on graft, and the capital lived under perennial flood terror.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆二年春，導索水自旃然，與須水合入於汴。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Jianlong under Emperor Taizu, the Suo River was led from Zhanran and combined with the Xu River to enter the Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Taizu's second Jianlong year, the Suo River was channeled from Zhanran to join the Xu and feed the Bian.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，詔：「緣汴河州縣長吏，常以春首課民夾岸植榆柳，以固堤防。」

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year, an edict: "Prefectural and county chiefs along the Bian Canal shall always at the turn of spring require the people to plant elm and willow on both banks to strengthen the dikes in protection."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year three, an edict ordered Bian Canal magistrates each spring to set the people planting elms and willows along both banks.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國二年七月，開封府言：「汴水溢壞開封大寧堤，浸民田，害稼。」

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Taiping Xingguo under Emperor Taizong, the Kaifeng prefecture said: "The Bian water overflowed and damaged the Daining dike of Kaifeng, soaking commoners' fields and harming the grain crop."
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's seventh month of Taiping Xingguo year two, Kaifeng reported the Bian had burst the Daining dike, flooding fields and ruining crops.

sentences.zh: 詔發懷、孟丁夫三千五百人塞之。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched 3,500 laborers from Huai and Meng to block it.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent 3,500 corvée workers from Huai and Meng to plug the breach.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，發軍士千人復汴口。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, a thousand soldiers were dispatched to restore the Bian mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year three a thousand troops restored the canal intake.

sentences.zh: 六月，宋州言：「寧陵縣河溢，堤決。」

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Song Prefecture said: "In Ningling County the river overflowed and the dike broke."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Songzhou reported that at Ningling the river had overflowed and broken the dike.

sentences.zh: 詔發宋、亳丁夫四千五百人，分遣使臣護役。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched 4,500 laborers from Song and Bo, dividing and sending mission officials to oversee the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand five hundred corvée laborers from Song and Bo were sent under dispatched commissioners.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，又決于宋城縣，以本州諸縣人夫三千五百人塞之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year, it broke again at Songcheng County; with human corvée from all counties of this prefecture numbering 3,500, they blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year four the river broke again at Songcheng; three thousand five hundred local laborers sealed it.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年六月，汴水決浚儀縣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Chunhua, the Bian water breached Junyi County.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Chunhua year two the Bian breached Junyi.

sentences.zh: 帝乘步輦出乾元門，宰相、樞密迎謁。

translations.literal: The emperor rode a litter palanquin out through the Qianyuan Gate; the chief counselor and Military Affairs commissioner came forward to greet and attend.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor walked a litter out the Qianyuan Gate; chancellor and Military Affairs commissioners met him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「東京養甲兵數十萬，居人百萬家，天下轉漕，仰給在此一渠水，朕安得不顧。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Eastern Capital raises several hundred thousand armored troops, houses a million families of inhabitants; the empire's transport and tribute depends on this one canal's water—how can I not attend to it?"
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Eastern Capital feeds hundreds of thousands of soldiers and a million households—the empire's transport hangs on this single ditch. How could I ignore it?"

sentences.zh: 車駕入泥淖中，行百餘步，從臣震恐。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage entered into mud and mire; it went more than a hundred paces; followers and ministers were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: The procession plunged into mud for more than a hundred paces; attendants trembled.

sentences.zh: 殿前都指揮使戴興叩頭懇請回馭，遂捧輦出泥淖中。

translations.literal: The Palace Front commander-in-chief Dai Xing kowtowed and earnestly begged to turn back the conveyance; thereupon he lifted the palanquin out of mud and mire.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Front commander Dai Xing kowtowed and pleaded for retreat, then bore the litter back to firm ground.

sentences.zh: 詔興督步卒數千塞之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xing to supervise several thousand infantry in blocking it.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was ordered to seal the breach with several thousand foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 日未旰，水勢遂定。

translations.literal: Before the sun had reached its height, the water's force at once settled.
translations.idiomatic: Before noon the water stilled.

sentences.zh: 帝始就次，太官進膳。

translations.literal: The emperor then took his seat; the Imperial Catering Office presented food.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then took refreshment from the Imperial Pantry.

sentences.zh: 親王近臣皆泥濘沾衣。

translations.literal: Princes of the imperial clan and close ministers all had mud splattered on their robes.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and close ministers stood filthy with mud.

sentences.zh: 知縣宋炎亡匿不敢出，特赦其罪。

translations.literal: The county magistrate Song Yan hid and fled and dared not come out; he was specially pardoned his crime.
translations.idiomatic: County magistrate Song Yan had fled in hiding; he received a special pardon.

sentences.zh: 是月，汴又決于宋城縣，發近縣丁夫二千人塞之。

translations.literal: That month the Bian also breached at Songcheng County; nearby counties' corvée laborers two thousand blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: That same month the Bian broke again at Songcheng; two thousand nearby corvée workers plugged it.

sentences.zh: 至道元年九月，帝以汴河歲運江、淮米五七百萬斛，以濟京師，問侍臣汴水疏鑿之由，令參知政事張洎講求其事以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Zhidao, the emperor because the Bian Canal each year transported Jiang and Huai grain of five to seven million hu to relieve the capital, asked attending ministers the origin of the Bian's dredging and opening, ordering Participating in Governance Zhang Bi to investigate the matter and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Zhidao year one, noting that the Bian yearly moved five to seven million bushels of Jianghuai grain to the capital, the emperor asked how the canal had been cut and ordered Zhang Bi to research and report.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：

translations.literal: His words said:
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bi answered:

sentences.zh: 禹導河自積石至龍門，南至華陰，東至砥柱；

translations.literal: Yu guided the river from Jishi to Longmen, south to Huayin, east to Dizhu;
translations.idiomatic: Yu channeled the river from Jishi to Longmen, south to Huayin, east to Dizhu;

sentences.zh: 又東至於孟津，東過洛汭，至於大伾，即今成皋是也，或云黎陽山也。

translations.literal: again east to Mengjin, east passing Luoyin, reaching Daqi—that is today's Chenggao, or so it is said Liyang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: then east to Mengjin and past Luoyin to Mount Daqi—today's Chenggao, also called Liyang Hill.

sentences.zh: 禹以大河流泛中國，為害最甚，乃于貝丘疏二渠，以分水勢：一渠自舞陽縣東，引入漯水，其水東北流，至千乘縣入海，即今黃河是也；

translations.literal: Yu because the Great River's flow spread broadly across China, causing harm most severely, then at Beiqiu dredged two canals to divide the water's force: one canal from east of Wuyang County drew into the Luo water; its water flowed northeast, reaching Qiansheng County to enter the sea—that is today's Yellow River;
translations.idiomatic: Because the river's vast floods ravaged the central plains, Yu at Beiqiu cut two canals to split its force: one east of Wuyang feeding the Luo, which ran northeast through Qiansheng to the sea—the present Yellow River;

sentences.zh: 一渠疏畎引傍西山，以東北形高敝壞堤，水勢不便流溢，夾右碣石入於渤海。

translations.literal: one canal dredged field ditches drawing along the western mountains; because to the northeast the terrain was high and could damage dikes, the water's force was inconvenient for overflowing flow, flanking Jieshi on the right to enter the Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: another drew field channels along the western hills; where northeastern terrain rose high enough to threaten dikes, overflow was checked and the stream was guided past Jieshi into the Bohai.

sentences.zh: 《書》所謂「北過洚水，至於大陸」，洚水即濁漳，大陸則邢州钜鹿澤。

translations.literal: What the Classic of Documents calls "north passing the Ji water, reaching the great plain"—Ji water is the muddy Zhang, the great plain is the Julu marsh of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents' "north past the Ji to the Great Plain" means the muddy Zhang and the Julu marsh of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 「播為九河，同為逆河，入於海。」

translations.literal: "Spread into nine rivers, together making the opposing river, entering the sea."
translations.idiomatic: "It was spread into nine channels, together forming the opposing river, and entered the sea."

sentences.zh: 河自魏郡貴鄉縣界分為九道，下至滄州，今為一河。

translations.literal: The river from the border of Guixiang County in Weijun divided into nine courses, below reaching Cangzhou; today it is one river.
translations.idiomatic: From Guixiang in Weijun it once split into nine branches down to Cangzhou; now only one remains.

sentences.zh: 言逆河者，謂與河水往復相承受也。

translations.literal: Speaking of the opposing river means that with the river water it goes back and forth mutually receiving and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: "Opposing river" describes how backwater and main current alternately receive each other.

sentences.zh: 齊桓公塞以廣田居，唯一河存焉，今其東界至莽梧河是也。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi blocked it to expand fields for settlement; only one river remained; today its eastern border reaches Mangwu River.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi dammed channels to reclaim farmland, leaving a single stream whose eastern limit today is the Mangwu River.

sentences.zh: 禹又於滎澤下分大河為陰溝，引注東南，以通淮、泗。

translations.literal: Yu again below Rong Marsh divided the Great River into the Yin Ditch, drawing and pouring southeast to connect Huai and Si.
translations.idiomatic: Yu also split the main river below Rong Marsh into the Yin Ditch toward the Huai and Si.

sentences.zh: 至大樑浚儀縣西北，復分為二渠：一渠元經陽武縣中牟台下為官渡水；

translations.literal: Reaching northwest of Daliang, Junyi County, it again divided into two canals: one canal originally passed Yangwu County below the Zhongmou terrace as Guandu water;
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of Daliang at Junyi it again forked: one branch ran under Zhongmou in Yangwu as Guandu water;

sentences.zh: 一渠始皇疏鑿以灌魏郡，謂之鴻溝，莨菪渠自滎陽五出池口來注之。

translations.literal: one canal the First Emperor dredged and cut to irrigate Weijun, called the Hong Ditch; the Langdang channel from five outlets at Chiyang in Xingyang came to pour into it.
translations.idiomatic: another was the First Emperor's Hong Ditch to irrigate Weijun, fed by the Langdang channel from five outlets at Chiyang in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 其鴻溝即出河之溝，亦曰莨菪渠。

translations.literal: That Hong Ditch is the ditch coming out of the river; it is also called the Langdang channel.
translations.idiomatic: The Hong Ditch is the river's outlet channel, also termed Langdang.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝時，樂浪人王景、謁者王吳始作浚儀渠，蓋循河溝故讀也。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming of Han, the Lelang man Wang Jing and the attendant Wang Wu first made the Junyi canal, broadly following the old course of the river ditch.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han Ming, Wang Jing of Lelang and attendant Wang Wu rebuilt the Junyi Canal along the old river trench.

sentences.zh: 渠成流注浚儀，故以浚儀縣為名。

translations.literal: When the canal was completed flow poured into Junyi; therefore it takes Junyi County as its name.
translations.idiomatic: When complete, its flow entered Junyi and took that county's name.

sentences.zh: 靈帝建寧四年，于敖城西北壘石為門，以遏渠口，故世謂之石門。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianning under Emperor Ling, at northwest of Aocheng stone was piled as a gate to check the canal mouth; therefore the age calls it Stone Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Ling's fourth Jianning year, masons piled a stone gate northwest of Aocheng to throttle the mouth—the Stone Gate of later ages.

sentences.zh: 渠外東合濟水，濟與河、渠渾濤東注，至敖山北，渠水至此又兼邲之水，即《春秋》晉、楚戰於邲。

translations.literal: Outside the canal to the east it joined the Ji water; Ji and river and canal turbidly roared eastward in pour; reaching north of Aoshan, at this place the canal water again combined with Bi water—that is the Jin–Chu battle at Bi in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: East of the canal it mingled with the Ji; river, canal, and Ji thundered eastward, and at Aoshan's north Bi water joined—the stream of the Jin–Chu battle at Bi.

sentences.zh: 邲又音汳，即「汴」字，古人避「反」字，改從「汴」字。

translations.literal: Bi again is pronounced bian, that is the character "Bian"; ancients avoided the character "fan" and changed to follow the character "Bian."
translations.idiomatic: Bi was also read bian—the origin of the character "Bian"; ancients shunned the homophone "fan" and wrote "Bian" instead.

sentences.zh: 渠水又東經滎陽北，旃然水自縣東流入汴水。

translations.literal: The canal water again passed east by north of Xingyang; Zhanran water from east of the county flowed into the Bian water.
translations.idiomatic: The canal ran east past Xingyang's north, where Zhanran water entered from the county's east.

sentences.zh: 鄭州滎陽縣西二十里三皇山上，有二廣武城，二城相去百餘步，汴水自兩城間小澗中東流而出，而濟流自茲乃絕。

translations.literal: Twenty li west of Xingyang County, Zhengzhou, on Sanguan Mountain are two Guangwu cities; the two cities are separated by a little more than a hundred paces; the Bian water from a small ravine between the two cities flowed east and out, while the Ji's flow from here then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li west of Xingyang stand twin Guangwu towns on Sanguan Hill a hundred paces apart; the Bian issued between them through a narrow gorge, and the Ji ended there.

sentences.zh: 唯汴渠首受旃然水，謂之鴻渠。

translations.literal: Only the Bian canal's head receives Zhanran water; it is called the Hong canal.
translations.idiomatic: The canal head takes only Zhanran water—then called the Hong Canal.

sentences.zh: 東晉太和中，桓溫北伐前燕，將通之，不果。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era of Eastern Jin, Huan Wen on northern expedition against Former Yan intended to open it but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In Eastern Jin's Taihe era Huan Wen, campaigning against Former Yan, tried to reopen it but failed.

sentences.zh: 義熙十三年，劉裕西征姚秦，復浚此渠，始有湍流奔注，而岸善潰塞，裕更疏鑿而漕運焉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yixi, Liu Yu on western expedition against Yao Qin again dredged this canal; only then was there swift rushing flow and pouring pour; yet the banks were good at collapsing and blocking, and Yu again dredged and cut so grain transport could proceed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yixi, Liu Yu, marching west against Yao Qin, dredged the channel again—swift water returned, though banks still collapsed until further cuts restored transport.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝大業三年，詔尚書左丞相皇甫誼發河南男女百萬開汴水，起滎澤入淮千餘里，乃為通濟渠。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye under Sui Emperor Yang, an edict ordered Left Director of the Secretariat Huangfu Yi to mobilize a million men and women of Henan to open the Bian water, starting from Rong Marsh entering the Huai for more than a thousand li; then it was made the Tongji Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui Yang's third Daye year, Left Chancellor Huangfu Yi conscripted a million Henan workers to open the Bian from Rong Marsh to the Huai—a thousand li—the Tongji Canal.

sentences.zh: 又發淮南兵夫十餘萬開邗溝，自山陽淮至於揚子江三百餘里，水面闊四十步，而後行幸焉。

translations.literal: Again ten-odd myriad Huainan soldier-laborers were dispatched to open the Han Ditch, from Huai at Shanyang to the Yangzi River more than three hundred li; water surface width forty paces; afterward the emperor went on tour.
translations.idiomatic: Another hundred thousand Huainan troops cut the Han Gou from the Huai at Shanyang to the Yangzi, three hundred li wide enough for forty paces, before Yang undertook his tours.

sentences.zh: 自後天下利於轉輸。

translations.literal: From afterward the empire profited in turning and transporting.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the realm reaped the benefits of long-distance transport.

sentences.zh: 昔孝文時，賈誼言「漢以江、淮為奉地」，謂魚、鹽、穀、帛，多出東南。

translations.literal: In former times under Emperor Xiaowen, Jia Yi said "Han takes the Jiang and Huai as its supply lands," meaning fish, salt, grain, and cloth mostly came from the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: As early as Emperor Wen’s reign, Jia Yi wrote that the Han took the Yangtze and Huai as its provisioning lands—fish, salt, grain, and cloth flowed chiefly from the southeast.

sentences.zh: 至五鳳中，耿壽昌奏：「故事，歲增關東谷四百萬斛以給京師。」

translations.literal: Reaching the Wufeng era, Geng Shouchang memorialized: "By precedent, each year four million hu of eastern-region grain were added to supply the capital."
translations.idiomatic: By the Wufeng reign period, Geng Shouchang reported that precedent called for shipping four million hu of eastern grain yearly to the capital.

sentences.zh: 亦多自此渠漕運。

translations.literal: Much also came by canal transport from this channel.
translations.idiomatic: Most of that grain, too, moved along this canal.

sentences.zh: 唐初，改通濟渠為廣濟渠。

translations.literal: Early Tang, changed the Tongji Canal to the Guangji Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tang the Tongji Canal was renamed the Guangji Canal.

sentences.zh: 開元中，黃門侍郎、平章事裴耀卿言：江、淮租船，自長淮西北溯鴻溝，轉相輸納于河陰、含嘉、太原等倉。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Grand Councilor Pei Yaoqing said: Yangtze–Huai tribute ships, from the long Huai northwest upstream through the Hong Gou, turning to deliver to Heyin, Hanjia, Taiyuan, and other granaries.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, Grand Councilor Pei Yaoqing noted that Jianghuai tribute fleets sailed northwest up the Hong Gou from the lower Huai and transshipped grain into granaries at Heyin, Hanjia, Taiyuan, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 凡三年，運米七百萬石，實利涉於此。

translations.literal: In all three years, transported rice seven million shi; real profit involved this.
translations.idiomatic: Over three years they moved seven million shi of rice—the gain lay in this route.

sentences.zh: 開元末，河南採訪使、汴州刺史齊浣，以江、淮漕運經淮水波濤有沉損，遂浚廣濟渠下流，自泗州虹縣至楚州淮陰縣北八十里合於淮，逾時畢功。

translations.literal: End of Kaiyuan, Henan Investigation Commissioner and Bianzhou Prefect Qi Huan, because Jiang–Huai canal transport passed Huai waves and had sinking losses, then dredged the Guangji Canal lower reaches, from Sizhou Hong County to Chuzhou Huaiyin County north eighty li joining the Huai, exceeding the allotted time yet completing the work.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaiyuan, Qi Huan of Henan and Bianzhou, seeing Jianghuai grain boats wrecked in Huai surf, dredged the lower Guangji from Hong in Sizhou to Huaiyin in Chuzhou—eighty li to the Huai—and finished, though past deadline.

sentences.zh: 既而水流迅急，行旅艱險，尋乃廢停，卻由舊河。

translations.literal: Soon after the water flow was swift and urgent, travelers difficult and dangerous; soon it was abandoned and stopped, returning by the old river.
translations.idiomatic: The current proved too swift for safe travel, so the cut was abandoned and traffic reverted to the old channel.

sentences.zh: 德宗朝，歲漕運江、淮米四十萬石，以益關中。

translations.literal: Under Dezong, each year canal transport of Jiang–Huai rice four hundred thousand shi, to augment Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Dezong’s reign four hundred thousand shi of Jianghuai rice were shipped annually to supply Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時叛將李正己、田悅皆分軍守徐州，臨渦口，梁崇義阻兵襄、鄧，南北漕引皆絕。

translations.literal: At the time rebel generals Li Zhengji and Tian Yue each divided armies guarding Xuzhou, overlooking the Woguo mouth; Liang Chongyi blocked troops at Xiang and Deng; north–south canal diversions were all cut.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel commanders Li Zhengji and Tian Yue held Xuzhou and the Woguo crossing; Liang Chongyi blocked Xiangyang and Dengzhou—north–south grain routes were severed.

sentences.zh: 於是水陸運使杜佑請改漕路，自浚儀西十里疏其南涯，引流入琵琶溝，經蔡河至陳州合潁水，是秦、漢故道，以官漕久不由此，故填淤不通，若畎流培岸，則功用甚寡；

translations.literal: Thereupon Water-and-Land Transport Commissioner Du You requested changing the canal route: from Junyi west ten li dredge its south bank, draw water into the Pipa Ditch, pass the Cai River to Chenzhou to join the Ying River—this is the Qin–Han old route; because official canal transport long had not used it, it was filled and silted and impassable; if irrigation flow and bank building, then labor would be very little;
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Du You proposed a new route: ten li west of Junyi, open the south bank into Pipa Ditch, follow the Cai to Chenzhou and the Ying—an ancient Qin–Han channel silted shut. Minor dredging and bank work, he argued, would reopen it cheaply;

sentences.zh: 又廬、壽之間有水道，而平岡亙其中，曰雞鳴山，佑請疏其兩端，皆可通舟，其間登陸四十里而已，則江、湖、黔、嶺、蜀、漢之粟，可方舟而下。

translations.literal: Also between Lu and Shou there is a waterway, but a level mound spans within, called Jiming Mountain; You requested dredging both ends so boats could pass; between them only forty li of land portage—then grain from the Jiang, lakes, Qian, Ling, Shu, and Han could go downstream in convoys.
translations.idiomatic: Between Luzhou and Shouzhou a level ridge called Jiming Hill blocked the waterway; Du You urged cutting both ends so only a forty-li portage remained, letting grain from the Yangtze basin, the southwest, and Hanzhong float down in fleets.

sentences.zh: 由是白沙趨東關，經廬、壽，浮潁步蔡，曆琵琶溝入汴河，不復經溯淮之險，徑于舊路二千里，功寡利博。

translations.literal: By this from Baisha toward Dongguan, passing Lu and Shou, floating on the Ying and walking the Cai, traversing Pipa Ditch into the Bian River, no longer passing the danger of upstream Huai, direct on the old route two thousand li—labor little, profit broad.
translations.idiomatic: Grain would run from Baisha to Dongguan, through Lu and Shou, down the Ying and Cai, into Pipa Ditch and the Bian—avoiding the Huai ascent yet saving two thousand li, with modest cost and great gain.

sentences.zh: 朝議將行，而徐州順命，淮路乃通。

translations.literal: Court discussion was about to implement it, but Xuzhou submitted to orders and the Huai route opened.
translations.idiomatic: The court was poised to adopt the plan when Xuzhou submitted and the Huai route reopened.

sentences.zh: 至國家膺圖受命，以大樑四方所湊，天下之樞，可以臨制四海，故卜京邑而定都。

translations.literal: When the state received the Mandate, with Daliang where the four quarters gather—the pivot of all under heaven, able to oversee the four seas—it therefore divined the capital and fixed the seat.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty took the Mandate, Daliang stood where the realm converged—a hub from which to command the four seas—so the court chose it and fixed the capital there.

sentences.zh: 漢高帝云：「吾以羽檄召天下兵未至。」

translations.literal: Han Gaozu said: "I summoned all-under-heaven’s troops with urgent dispatch, yet they did not arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu once said, “I called the empire’s armies with urgent dispatches, and they still did not come.”

sentences.zh: 孝文又云：「吾初即位，不欲出虎符召郡國兵。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen again said: "At my first accession I did not wish to issue tiger tallies summoning commandery and kingdom troops."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen added, “When I first took the throne I would not even issue tiger tallies to summon the commanderies.”

sentences.zh: 即知兵甲在外也。

translations.literal: From this one knows armor and weapons were outside.
translations.idiomatic: Both remarks show that real military power lay in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 唯有南北軍、期門郎、羽林孤兒，以備天子扈從藩衛之用。

translations.literal: Only the Northern and Southern Armies, Qimen guards, and Yulin orphans remained, to prepare the Son of Heaven’s escort and frontier guard.
translations.idiomatic: Only the capital guards—the Northern and Southern Armies, the Qimen, and the Yulin cadets—served as the emperor’s personal escort.

sentences.zh: 唐承隋制，置十二衛府兵，皆農夫也。

translations.literal: Tang inherited the Sui system, establishing twelve guard frontier troops, all of them farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Tang kept Sui’s twelve guard units of farmer-soldiers.

sentences.zh: 及罷府兵，始置神武、神策為禁軍，不過三數萬人，亦以備扈從藩衛而已，故祿山犯關，驅市人而戰；

translations.literal: When frontier troops were abolished, Shenwu and Shence were first established as forbidden armies—no more than thirty-odd thousand men—also only to prepare escort and frontier guard; therefore when Lushan violated the pass he drove market people to battle;
translations.idiomatic: After the frontier armies were dissolved, the Shenwu and Shence formed a palace guard of barely thirty thousand—enough for escort duty alone, so when An Lushan stormed the pass he had to press townsfolk into battle;

sentences.zh: 德宗蒙塵，扈駕四百餘騎，兵甲皆在郡國。

translations.literal: Dezong, covered in dust on the road, had barely four hundred riders in escort; armor and weapons were all in the commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: and when Dezong fled the capital his escort numbered four hundred horsemen while arms and armor sat in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 額軍存而可舉者，除河朔三鎮外，太原、青社各十萬人，邠甯、宣武各六萬人，潞、徐、荊、揚各五萬人，襄、宣、壽、鎮海各二萬人，自餘觀察、團練據要害之地者，不下萬人。

translations.literal: Of border troops existing and summonable, besides the three Hebei circuits, Taiyuan and Qing–She each had a hundred thousand, Binning and Xuanwu each sixty thousand, Lu, Xu, Jing, and Yang each fifty thousand, Xiang, Xuan, Shou, and Zhenhai each twenty thousand; the remaining observation and training regiments holding strategic places were not below ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Deployable frontier forces—aside from the three Hebei circuits—numbered about one hundred thousand each at Taiyuan and Qingqi, sixty thousand at Binning and Xuanwu, fifty thousand at Lu, Xu, Jing, and Yang, twenty thousand at Xiang, Xuan, Shou, and Zhenhai, and at least ten thousand at every other strategic garrison.

sentences.zh: 今天下甲卒數十萬眾，戰馬數十萬匹，並萃京師，悉集七亡國之士民於輦下，比漢、唐京邑，民庶十倍。

translations.literal: Today armor and troops several hundred thousand masses and war horses several hundred thousand, all gathered at the capital, all collecting the gentry and people of seven perished states under the imperial carriage—compared with Han and Tang capitals, common people tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: Now hundreds of thousands of soldiers and horses crowd the capital, with subjects from seven conquered kingdoms packed under the throne—a population ten times that of Han or Tang Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 甸服時有水旱，不至艱歉者，有惠民、金水、五丈、汴水等四渠，派引脈分，鹹會天邑，舳艫相接，贍給公私。

translations.literal: When the crown domain suffered flood or drought it did not reach hardship and famine, because the Huimin, Jinshui, Wuzhang, and Bian canals branched and divided, all converging on the heavenly capital; ships stem to stern connected, supplying public and private needs.
translations.idiomatic: Flood and drought in the capital region rarely brought famine: four canals—the Huimin, Jinshui, Wuzhang, and Bian—fed the city in an unbroken line of barges for public and private stores alike.

sentences.zh: 所以無匱乏，唯汴水橫亙中國，首承大河，漕引江、湖，利盡南海，半天下之財賦，並山澤之百貨，悉由此路而進。

translations.literal: Therefore without shortage: only the Bian water spans China, its head receiving the Great River, canal drawing the Jiang and lakes, profit reaching the South Sea; half of all-under-heaven’s wealth and levies, together with mountains’ and marshes’ hundred goods, all entered by this route.
translations.idiomatic: The capital never wanted for goods because the Bian crossed the empire, took the Yellow River at its head, drew the Yangtze and lakes, and reached the southern sea—half the realm’s taxes and every mountain and marsh product came this way.

sentences.zh: 然則禹力疏鑿以分水勢，煬帝開畎以奉巡遊，雖數湮廢，而通流不絕於百代之下，終為國家之用者，其上天之意乎？

translations.literal: Then Yu by strength dredged and cut to divide water force; Yangdi opened irrigation channels to support his tours—though several times silted and abandoned, flow never ceased under a hundred generations, ultimately serving the state: was this heaven’s intent?
translations.idiomatic: Yu had split the waters by dredging; Yang of Sui had cut channels for his tours—time and again they silted up, yet the current never failed the dynasty for long. Perhaps heaven meant the Bian to endure.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年八月，汴水漲溢，自京至鄭州，浸道路。

translations.literal: Second year, eighth month of Dazhong Xiangfu: the Bian water rose and overflowed from the capital to Zhengzhou, inundating the roads.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second Xiangfu year (1009) the Bian flooded from the capital to Zhengzhou and covered the highways.

sentences.zh: 詔選使乘傳減汴口水勢。

translations.literal: An edict selected envoys with relay horses to reduce the Bian mouth’s water force.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent fast couriers to lower the headworks at the Bian intake.

sentences.zh: 既而水減，阻滯漕運，復遣浚汴口。

translations.literal: Soon after the water fell, grain transport was blocked, and they again sent men to dredge the Bian mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When the level dropped and barges stalled, officials dredged the intake again.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，詔自今後汴水添漲及七尺五寸，即遣禁兵三千，沿河防護。

translations.literal: Sixth month of the eighth year: an edict ordered that whenever the Bian rose seven chi five cun, three thousand forbidden troops were to guard the banks.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year eight (1015) the throne ruled that a rise of seven and a half chi on the Bian would trigger three thousand palace guards along the levees.

sentences.zh: 八月，太常少卿馬元方請浚汴河中流，闊五丈，深五尺，可省修堤之費。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Director of Ceremonies Vice Minister Ma Yuanfang requested dredging the Bian’s mid-channel five zhang wide and five chi deep to save dike-repair costs.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Ma Yuanfang urged cutting the mid-reach five zhang wide and five chi deep so dikes could be trimmed.

sentences.zh: 即詔遣使計度修浚。

translations.literal: An edict immediately sent envoys to calculate and dredge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a survey and dredging at once.

sentences.zh: 使還，上言：「泗州西至開封府界，岸闊底平，水勢薄，不假開浚。

translations.literal: The envoy returned and reported: "From Sizhou west to the Kaifeng boundary the banks are broad, the bed flat, and the current light—no dredging needed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reported that from Sizhou west to Kaifeng the channel was wide, shallow, and calm—dredging unnecessary there.

sentences.zh: 請止自泗州夾岡，用功八十六萬五千四百三十八，以宿、亳丁夫充，計減功七百三十一萬，仍請於沿河作頭踏道擗岸，其淺處為鋸牙，以束水勢，使其浚成河道，止用河清、下卸卒，就未放春水前，令逐州長吏、令佐督役。

translations.literal: Request work only from the Sizhou ridge section, labor 865,438 using corvée from Su and Bo, calculating a reduction of 7.31 million work units; still request along the river building head stepping-paths and split banks, shallow places with saw-teeth to bind the current, completing the dredged channel using only River-Clear and Lower-Unload troops before the spring flood, with each prefecture’s chief and magistrate assistants supervising labor.
translations.idiomatic: Dredging should begin at the Sizhou hills—865,438 corvée days from Suzhou and Bozhou, saving 7.31 million units overall. Along the reach they should build towpaths, notch the banks, and set saw-tooth groins to pinch the flow; River-Clear and Lower-Unload crews must finish before the spring rise under local magistrates’ supervision.

sentences.zh: 自今汴河淤澱，可三五年一浚。

translations.literal: From now on Bian canal silt might be dredged every three to five years.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Bian would be dredged every few years as needed.

sentences.zh: 又于中牟、滎澤縣各置開減水河。」

translations.literal: Also at Zhongmou and Xing Marsh counties each establish flood-reduction rivers."
translations.idiomatic: Flood-relief cuts were also ordered at Zhongmou and Xing Marsh.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved everything.

sentences.zh: 天禧三年十二月，都官員外郎鄭希甫言：「汴河兩岸皆是陂水，廣浸民田，堤腳並無流泄之處。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, third year of Tianxi: Director of Ministries Vice Minister Zheng Xifu said: "Both banks of the Bian are ponded water broadly inundating common fields; at the dike foot there is no place for drainage.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Tianxi 3 (1019) Zheng Xifu reported that ponds along both Bian banks were flooding fields with nowhere to drain at the toe of the levee.

sentences.zh: 今汴河南省自明河接澳入淮，望詔轉運使規度以聞。」

translations.literal: Now south of the Bian in Henan, from the Ming River connect the Ao into the Huai—may the transport commissioner plan and report."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the transport commissioner survey linking the Ming River and Ao into the Huai south of the canal and report back."

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖三年，汴流淺，特遣使疏河注口。

translations.literal: Third year of Tiansheng under Renzong: the Bian ran shallow; an envoy was specially sent to dredge the river intake.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiansheng 3 (1025) the Bian ran low and the court sent a special mission to clear the intake.

sentences.zh: 四年，大漲，堤危，眾情恟忄匈憂京城，詔度京城西賈陂岡地，泄之于護龍河。

translations.literal: Fourth year: a great rise endangered the dikes; the crowd was alarmed and anxious for the capital; an edict measured mound land west of the capital and discharged water into the Hulong River.
translations.idiomatic: The next year a flood threatened the levees and panic gripped the capital; officials cut a spill west of the city into the Hulong River.

sentences.zh: 六年，勾當汴口康得輿言：「行視陽武橋萬勝鎮，宜存斗門。

translations.literal: Sixth year: Bian-mouth superintendent Kang Deyu said: "On inspection at Yangwu Bridge and Wansheng town, the sluice gates should be kept.
translations.idiomatic: In year six Kang Deyu, overseer of the Bian intake, argued after inspection that sluices at Yangwu Bridge and Wansheng must stay open.

sentences.zh: 其梁固斗門三宜廢去，祥符界北岸請為別竇，分減溢流。」

translations.literal: The three Lianggu sluice gates should be abolished; on the north bank at the Xiangfu boundary request a separate culvert to divide and reduce overflow."
translations.idiomatic: Three gates at Lianggu should close, he said, while a new culvert on the Xiangfu north bank would bleed off excess flow."

sentences.zh: 而勾當汴口王中庸欲增置孫村之石限，悉從其請。

translations.literal: But Bian-mouth superintendent Wang Zhongyong wished to add a stone weir at Sun Village—all their requests were followed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongyong, his counterpart, wanted a stone weir at Sun Village; the court granted both plans.

sentences.zh: 七年，德輿言，修河芟地為並灘農戶所侵。

translations.literal: Seventh year: Deyu said land cleared for river work had been encroached on by farmers on the combined beach.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven Deyu reported farmers seizing river-maintenance land on the floodplain.

sentences.zh: 詔限一月使自實，檢括以還縣官。

translations.literal: An edict gave one month for self-reporting truth; officials were to check and return holdings to the county.
translations.idiomatic: They had one month to confess encroachments before surveyors restored the land to the state.

sentences.zh: 皇祐三年，命使詣中牟治堤。

translations.literal: Third year of Huangyou: an envoy was ordered to Zhongmou to repair dikes.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangyou 3 (1051) the court sent an officer to repair Zhongmou’s levees.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，河涸，舟不通，令河渠司自口浚治，歲以為常。

translations.literal: Next year, eighth month: the river dried and boats could not pass; the Canal Bureau was ordered to dredge from the mouth yearly as a standing rule.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn the channel dried up; the Canal Bureau was told to dredge the intake annually thereafter.

sentences.zh: 舊制，水增七尺五寸，則京師集禁兵、八作、排岸兵，負土列河上以防河。

translations.literal: Old regulation: when water rose seven chi five cun, the capital gathered forbidden troops, Eight Works, and bank-defense troops to carry earth in lines along the river against flood.
translations.idiomatic: By old rule a seven-and-a-half-chi rise mobilized palace guards, artisans, and bank troops to heap earth along the levee.

sentences.zh: 滿五日，賜錢以勞之，曰「特支」；

translations.literal: After five days they received a cash bonus called "special disbursement";
translations.idiomatic: After five days they received a bonus called the "special payout";

sentences.zh: 而或數漲數防，又不及五日而罷，則軍士屢疲，而賜予不及。

translations.literal: yet sometimes floods rose and fell several times before five days ended, so soldiers grew weary while rewards never came.
translations.idiomatic: but repeated surges often ended the emergency before five days, leaving men exhausted and unpaid.

sentences.zh: 是歲七月，始制防河兵日給錢，薄其數，才比特支十分之一，軍士便之。

translations.literal: Seventh month of that year: a daily wage for flood troops was first instituted—smaller than the special payout, only about a tenth—and the soldiers welcomed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year daily flood pay was introduced—one-tenth of the old bonus—and troops approved.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣使行河相利害。

translations.literal: The next year an envoy was sent to travel the river and assess benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an inspector toured the canal to weigh costs and gains.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐六年，汴水淺澀，常稽運漕。

translations.literal: Sixth year of Jiayou: the Bian ran shallow and sluggish, often delaying grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 6 (1061) low, sluggish water on the Bian repeatedly delayed tribute fleets.

sentences.zh: 都水奏：「河自應天府抵泗州，直流湍駛無所阻。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Waterways memorialized: "From Yingtian prefecture to Sizhou the current runs straight and swift without obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate reported that from Yingtian to Sizhou the current was swift and unobstructed.

sentences.zh: 惟應天府上至汴口，或岸闊淺漫，宜限以六十步闊，於此則為木岸狹河，扼束水勢令深駛。

translations.literal: Only from Yingtian up to the Bian mouth are banks sometimes broad and shallow; they should be limited to sixty bu in width so wooden revetments narrow the channel, choke the current, and make it deep and fast.
translations.idiomatic: Only the reach above Yingtian to the intake was wide and shallow; narrowing it to sixty paces with timber revetments would pinch the flow and deepen the channel.

sentences.zh: 梢，伐岸木可足也。」

translations.literal: Shao—cutting bank timber—would suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Timber cut from the banks would supply the revetments.

sentences.zh: 遂下詔興役，而眾議以為未便。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered the work, but public debate held it unwise.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the project, though many called it ill-advised.

sentences.zh: 宰相蔡京奏：「祖宗時已嘗狹河矣，俗好沮敗事，宜勿聽。」

translations.literal: Chancellor Cai Jing memorialized: "The ancestors already narrowed the river once; the vulgar love to obstruct good works—do not listen."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing urged the emperor to ignore critics: “Our forebears already narrowed the channel; common talk always blocks useful work.”

sentences.zh: 役既半，岸木不足，募民出雜梢。

translations.literal: When the work was half done bank timber ran short and commoners were recruited to supply mixed shao.
translations.idiomatic: Midway through, timber ran short and civilians were hired to furnish mixed revetment poles.

sentences.zh: 岸成而言者始息。

translations.literal: When the banks were finished the critics at last fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Once the revetments stood, opposition died away.

sentences.zh: 舊曲灘漫流，多稽留覆溺處，悉為駛直平夷，操舟往來便之。

translations.literal: Old curved shallows where spreading flow caused delays and capsizing were all made swift, straight, and level, so boatmen passed conveniently.
translations.idiomatic: Former bends that had slowed and sunk boats were straightened, and traffic eased.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧四年，創開訾家口，日役夫四萬，饒一月而成。

translations.literal: Fourth year of Xining under Shenzong: the Zijia intake was newly opened; forty thousand laborers worked daily and finished in a month.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 4 (1071) the court cut the Zijia intake with forty thousand laborers a day and finished in a month.

sentences.zh: 才三月已淺澱，乃復開舊口，役萬工，四日而水稍順。

translations.literal: In only three months it had silted shallow; they reopened the old mouth with ten thousand workers, and after four days the water ran somewhat smoothly.
translations.idiomatic: Within three months it silted shut; reopening the old mouth with ten thousand men restored a modest current in four days.

sentences.zh: 有應舜臣者，獨謂新口在孤柏嶺下，當河流之沖，其便利可常用勿易，水大則泄以斗門，水小則為輔渠於下流以益之。

translations.literal: Ying Shunchen alone said the new mouth below Gubai Ridge lay in the river’s main rush and should be kept permanently; when water was high discharge through sluice gates, when low build an auxiliary canal downstream to supplement it.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shunchen alone argued that the new cut below Gubai Ridge sat in the main current and should stay open—sluices for floods, a feeder ditch in drought.

sentences.zh: 安石善其議。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi endorsed the plan.

sentences.zh: 五年，先是，宣徽北院使、中太一宮使張方平嘗論汴河曰：「國家漕運，以河渠為主。

translations.literal: Fifth year: earlier, Director of the Palace Northern Court and Commissioner of the Zhongtaiyi Palace Zhang Fangping had discussed the Bian River, saying: "State grain transport takes river canals as its foundation.
translations.idiomatic: In year five Zhang Fangping—palace commissioner and Zhongtaiyi envoy—had warned: “Imperial transport rests on the canals.

sentences.zh: 國初浚河渠三道，通京城漕運，自後定立上供年額：汴河斛鬥六百萬石，廣濟河六十二萬石，惠民河六十萬石。

translations.literal: At the founding three canal routes were dredged for capital transport; afterward fixed annual tribute quotas were set: Bian Canal six million hu, Guangji Canal 620,000 hu, Huimin Canal 600,000 hu.
translations.idiomatic: The founders opened three routes to the capital and fixed quotas: six million hu on the Bian, 620,000 on the Guangji, 600,000 on the Huimin.

sentences.zh: 廣濟河所運，止給太康、咸平、尉氏等縣軍糧而已。

translations.literal: Guangji Canal transport only supplied military grain for Taikang, Xianping, Weishi, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangji fed only garrisons around Taikang, Xianping, and Weishi.

sentences.zh: 惟汴河專運粳米，兼以小麥，此乃大倉蓄積之實。

translations.literal: Only the Bian Canal solely transported polished rice together with wheat—this is the Great Granary’s stored substance.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Bian carried polished rice and wheat—the substance of the Great Granary.

sentences.zh: 今仰食於官廩者，不惟三軍，至於京師士庶以億萬計，太半待飽於軍稍之餘，故國家於漕事至急至重。

translations.literal: Today those depending on official granaries are not only the three armies; reaching the capital’s gentry and common people by the hundreds of millions, the greater half await full bellies on army grain surplus—therefore the state toward transport is utmost urgent and utmost heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Millions in the capital, not just the armies, live on surplus transport grain; the dynasty’s fate hangs on the canal.

sentences.zh: 然則汴河乃建國之本，非可與區區溝洫水利同言也。

translations.literal: Then the Bian River is the founding state’s root—not to be spoken of in the same breath as trivial ditches and irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian is the dynasty’s lifeline—not some local irrigation ditch.

sentences.zh: 近歲已罷廣濟河，而惠民河斛鬥不入大倉，大眾之命，惟汴河是賴。

translations.literal: In recent years the Guangji Canal has been abolished and Huimin Canal grain does not enter the Great Granary; the masses’ lives rely only on the Bian River.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangji had been shut and Huimin grain no longer reached the central stores; the people depended solely on the Bian.

sentences.zh: 今陳說利害，以汴河為議者多矣。

translations.literal: Now those stating benefit and harm with the Bian River as their topic are many.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials debating the Bian had multiplied.

sentences.zh: 臣恐議者不已，屢作改更，必致汴河日失其舊。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that if discussers do not cease and repeatedly make changes, the Bian River must daily lose its old course.
translations.idiomatic: If debate never ends and plans keep changing, the canal will erode year by year.

sentences.zh: 國家大計，殊非小事。

translations.literal: The state’s great plan is especially not a small matter.
translations.idiomatic: This is no minor affair of hydraulics—it is national policy.

sentences.zh: 願陛下特回聖鑒，深賜省察，留神遠慮，以固基本。」

translations.literal: May Your Majesty especially turn the sage mirror, deeply bestow examination, retain mind for far consideration, and solidify the foundation."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to look far, examine deeply, and secure the foundation of the realm."

sentences.zh: 方平之言，為王安石發也。

translations.literal: Fangping’s words were aimed at Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang’s memorial was aimed at Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，都水監丞侯叔獻乞引汴水淤府界閒田，安石力主之。

translations.literal: Summer of the sixth year: Directorate of Waterways Assistant Supervisor Hou Shuxian requested drawing Bian water to silt vacant fields in the capital boundary; An Shi strongly supported it.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Hou Shuxian proposed flooding suburban fields with Bian water; Wang Anshi backed him firmly.

sentences.zh: 水既數放，或至絕流，公私重舟不可蕩，有閣折者。

translations.literal: Water was released several times and sometimes cut off flow entirely; public and private heavy boats could not swing; some were stranded and broken.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated draw-downs sometimes dried the channel; heavy barges grounded and some were wrecked.

sentences.zh: 帝以人情不安，嘗下都水分析，並詔三司同府界提點官往視。

translations.literal: The emperor, because popular feelings were uneasy, once ordered the Directorate of Waterways to analyze the matter and also issued an edict the Three Departments together with capital-boundary supervisory officials to go inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Public alarm moved the emperor to order analysis by the Directorate and a joint inspection by the Three Departments and capital commissioners.

sentences.zh: 十一月，範子奇建議：冬不閉汴口，以外江綱運直入汴至京，廢運般。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Fan Ziqi proposed: in winter do not close the Bian mouth; let outer-river convoys enter the Bian directly to the capital and abolish transshipment porters.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Fan Ziqi urged leaving the Bian mouth open through winter so sea-route fleets could sail straight to the capital, ending relay labor.

sentences.zh: 安石以為然。

translations.literal: An Shi thought it correct.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔汴口官吏相視，卒用其說。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Bian-mouth officials to inspect together; they finally used his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Intake officers surveyed the scheme and the court adopted it.

sentences.zh: 是後高麗入貢，令溯汴赴闕。

translations.literal: After this, when Goryeo sent tribute they were ordered to ascend the Bian to court.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Goryeo tribute missions were told to sail up the Bian to the capital.

sentences.zh: 七年春，河水壅溢，積潦敗堤。

translations.literal: Spring of the seventh year: river water blocked and overflowed; accumulated floodwaters ruined dikes.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year seven floodwater backed up and burst the levees.

sentences.zh: 八月，御史盛陶謂汴河開兩口非便，命同判都水監宋昌言視兩口水勢，檄同提舉汴口官王珫。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Censor Sheng Tao said opening two Bian mouths was not convenient; he ordered Associate Directorate of Waterways Song Changyan to inspect both mouths’ water force and document Bian-mouth raising official Wang Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Censor Sheng Tao attacked the twin intakes and had Song Changyan measure both flows with intake officer Wang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 珫言訾家口水三分，輔渠七分。

translations.literal: Xiu said Zijia mouth carried three-tenths of the water and the auxiliary canal seven-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu reported the Zijia cut took three-tenths of the flow and the feeder seven-tenths.

sentences.zh: 昌言請塞訾家口，而留輔渠。

translations.literal: Changyan requested blocking the Zijia mouth yet retaining the auxiliary canal.
translations.idiomatic: Song Changyan urged sealing Zijia while keeping the feeder ditch.

sentences.zh: 時韓絳、呂惠卿當國，許之。

translations.literal: At the time Han Jiang and Lü Huiqing held the state; it was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang and Lü Huiqing, then in power, approved.

sentences.zh: 八年春，安石再相，叔獻言：「昨疏浚汴河，自南京至泗州，概深三尺至五尺。

translations.literal: Spring of the eighth year: An Shi was again chancellor; Shuxian said: "Yesterday we dredged the Bian River from Nanjing to Sizhou, overall deepening three to five chi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year eight, with Wang Anshi back as chancellor, Hou Shuxian reported dredging the Bian from Nanjing to Sizhou to a depth of three to five chi throughout.

sentences.zh: 惟虹縣以東，有礓石三十里餘，不可疏浚，乞募民開修。」

translations.literal: Only east of Hong County there is rocky ground thirty-odd li that cannot be dredged; I beg to recruit commoners to open and repair it."
translations.idiomatic: East of Hong, he noted, thirty li of bedrock resisted dredging and asked for civilian contractors to cut through."

sentences.zh: 詔檢計工糧以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered inspection and calculation of labor and grain to report.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a cost survey.

sentences.zh: 七月，叔獻又言：「歲開汴口作生河，侵民田，調夫役。

translations.literal: Seventh month: Shuxian again said: "Each year opening the Bian mouth makes a living channel that invades common fields and adjusts corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Hou added that annual intake cuts flooded fields and tied up corvée.

sentences.zh: 今惟用訾家口，減人夫、物料各以萬計，乞減河清一指揮。」

translations.literal: Now using only the Zijia mouth reduces laborers and materials each by tens of thousands; I beg to reduce one River-Clear command."
translations.idiomatic: Relying solely on Zijia would save tens of thousands in labor and supplies, he said, and asked to cut one River-Clear regiment."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，汴水大漲，至深一丈二尺，於是復請權閉汴口。

translations.literal: Before long the Bian water rose greatly to a depth of one zhang two chi; they therefore again requested temporarily closing the Bian mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a twelve-chi flood forced them to seek a temporary closure of the intake.

sentences.zh: 九年十月，詔都水度量疏浚汴河淺深，仍記其地分。

translations.literal: Tenth month, ninth year: an edict ordered the Directorate of Waterways to measure dredging depths on the Bian and record each section.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year nine the Directorate was told to sound the Bian and log depths by section.

sentences.zh: 十年，範子淵請用濬川杷，以六月興工，自謂功利灼然，請「候今冬疏浚畢，將杷具、舟船等分給逐地分。

translations.literal: Tenth year: Fan Ziyuan requested using the Junchuan rake; work would start in the sixth month; he claimed merit and profit were obvious, and asked: "Wait until this winter’s dredging is finished, then distribute rake tools and boats to each place division.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten Fan Ziyuan proposed deploying the Junchuan dredge rake from the sixth month, boasting clear returns, and asked that after winter dredging "rake gear and boats be allotted by district.

sentences.zh: 使臣於閉口之後，檢量河道淤澱去處，至春水接續疏導」。

translations.literal: Let envoys after the mouth is closed inspect where the channel is silted and removed, and continue dredging when spring water comes."
translations.idiomatic: Envoys should then survey silt after the intake closed and resume cutting when the spring freshet arrived.

sentences.zh: 大抵皆無甚利。

translations.literal: Mostly all brought little profit.
translations.idiomatic: Few of these schemes paid off.

sentences.zh: 已而清汴之役興。

translations.literal: Before long the campaign to clear the Bian was launched.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the great Clear-Bian project began.
